source.title: Are We Recovering Mechanisms? Objective-Level Recovery Gaps in Mechanistic Interpretability
source.authors: Chu-Qin Geng; Li Zhang; Hao-Lin Ye; Mark Zhang; Lu-Ke Zhang; Xu-Jie Si

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study challenges the adequacy of intervention-based faithfulness as evidence of circuit recovery. It tests whether equally sized IOI circuits are ranked by faithfulness in line with their held-out behavior, and shows that rankings change with intervention and scoring metric.
record.gate_note: The study uses IOI as one task in its Human suite. It reports held-out answer agreement for the published reference and discovered candidates, pairwise misranking rates, and selected context-restoration results. It does not test the named head classes or their individual causal roles. Other tasks and cited findings are not included as IOI rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the published IOI circuit (as a 963-edge mask) in GPT-2 small as a reference. It measures its held-out answer agreement and shows that, in IOI, intervention-based faithfulness rankings of equal-size circuits change with the ablation type (resampling, mean, zero) and the metric (KL, LD, PD). This bears directly on V5. The 99% held-out agreement bears narrowly on V1's faithfulness part. The study does not test head classes, backup heads, other models, circuit overlap across methods, or prompt variants.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that intervention-based faithfulness can prefer an equally sized circuit with worse held-out behavior. This happens without any discovery algorithm, among EAP, EAP-IG, ACDC and Edge-SP outputs, under ordinary resampling, and under KL, LD and PD alike. They attribute this partly to context distortion: restoring selected intact-model signals reversed 96 of 100 persistent misrankings. They state that they show a ranking failure relative to behavior, not mechanism identity.
record.recipe_differences: Uses edge-mask circuits for IOI and compares equal-size candidates by intervention-based KL, LD, and PD faithfulness against held-out intact-model answer agreement. It does not reproduce the original head-by-head causal-role, completeness, or minimality tests; it uses the published circuit as a reference and controlled comparison point.
record.method_sensitivity: Faithfulness rankings vary with intervention: resampling, mean replacement, and zero replacement. Rankings also vary with scoring metric (KL, LD, PD). The study fixes IOI to the saved ABBA template and does not test prompt-distribution sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Pooled over the four Human-suite tasks, KL faithfulness under resampling prefers the behaviorally worse of two equal-size discovered circuits in 13.2–24.4% of candidate–candidate pairs, depending on method (EAP, EAP-IG, ACDC, Edge-SP).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Intervention-based faithfulness misranks equal-size circuits returned by automated discovery methods across tasks.

record.problems: The behavioral criterion is agreement with intact-model answers under ordinary resampling, which the authors say does not prove mechanism identity. IOI evaluation uses 100 validation prompts and 100 disjoint test prompts from a fixed ABBA template. The context-restoration cohort is selected from persistent misrankings and the search is bounded; the authors do not run matched random controls or test minimality of restorations. Uncertainty estimation is described, but uncertainty values are not stated for the IOI rates recorded here.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for other Human-suite tasks or InterpBench tasks, because they are not IOI results. The paper reports additional pooled cross-metric and context-restoration summaries, but these aggregate across tasks and are not IOI-specific; the IOI-specific restoration result is retained as ioi-restore.

untested.parts: The 26 heads, 7 classes and their roles; the original completeness and minimality tests. Only held-out answer agreement of an edge-mask version of the circuit is measured.
All: no ablation of name-mover heads and no test of backup heads.
All: only GPT-2 small, with no other sizes, checkpoints or reuse for other tasks.
All: no overlap between circuits found by different methods, ablations or metrics is measured.
Prompt-distribution dependence (a fixed ABBA template is used), and the fraction of logit difference or behavior the circuit explains under the original metric.
All: only the saved ABBA template, with no name-order, template or name-count variation.

missing.what: IOI-specific KL misranking among discovery outputs. Under mean ablation, 29/30 EAP and 30/30 ACDC candidates outscore the published IOI circuit; under resampling, 23/30 EAP-IG candidates do. Candidate–candidate counts are 119, 121, 106, 41 /435 under resampling.
IOI-specific LD/PD misranking among discovery outputs. Under zero ablation, 23–30/30 candidates from every method outscore the reference.
Mean held-out Q of IOI edited candidates falls as more reference edges are swapped: 98.96% at 1 edit, 86.98% at 10%, 66.16% at 20%, 47.73% at 75%.
IOI KL misranking by edit band. Mean-ablation reference–candidate misranking is 2/30 at 1 edit, 25/30 at 5% and 0/30 at 50%.

record.verdict_notes: The 24 discovery rows (ioi-eap/eapig/acdc/edgesp-*) are mislabeled as IOI but are Table 5 Human-suite pools. IOI values are in Tables 17 and 18. The IOI circuit is evaluated as a 963-edge mask, not head-level, so its relation to the original head circuit is assumed. Q is top-answer agreement, which is lenient: the 99% figure does not contradict V5's 'explains only part', which concerns logit difference. No label is given for that part.

versions.untested_parts: Tests behavioral agreement and faithfulness rankings for the published IOI reference and equal-size alternatives; does not test the 26-head composition, the seven head classes and their stated roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a joint mechanistic account.
No targeted ablation of main name-mover heads or test of self-repair by backup heads.
Does not test whether the same circuit or roles occur in other model sizes or checkpoints, or whether IOI components are reused for other tasks.

Tests whether faithfulness rankings depend on intervention and scoring metric, including for outputs of several discovery methods. It does not assess circuit overlap or establish whether different discovery methods recover essentially the same circuit.

Tests intervention and metric sensitivity and behavioral agreement for fixed evaluation prompts. It does not vary the IOI prompt distribution or establish a general fraction of model behavior explained by the circuit.
IOI uses a fixed saved ABBA template; the study does not vary name order, templates, or number of names.
